title: The Standard of Ur
blurb: Compare the War side and the Peace side of a mosaic box from a royal tomb, and find what it reveals about Sumerian kings, armies and trade.

title: The Great Ziggurat of Ur
blurb: Climb the triple stairway of the moon god's temple-mountain, rebuilt as it may have looked when new, and ask why kings built mountains for gods.

title: The Law Stele of Hammurabi
blurb: Walk around a real 3D scan of the stone that carries Hammurabi's 282 laws, and decide whether 'an eye for an eye' was justice for everyone.

title: The Narmer Palette
blurb: Turn over the carved stone that shows King Narmer in the crowns of Upper and Lower Egypt, and decide whether it records a real war or a message about kingship.

title: The Bust of Nefertiti
blurb: Explore the Berlin museum's own full-colour scan of the queen's painted bust, and decide who should own it today.

title: Tutankhamun's Chariot
blurb: Walk around one of the six chariots buried with Tutankhamun, the high-speed war machine of New Kingdom Egypt.

title: The Gold Mask of Tutankhamun
era: Ancient Egypt · New Kingdom, about 1323 BCE
blurb: Turn the boy king's funerary mask, read its symbols, and decide what it tells us about Egyptian beliefs about death and kingship.

title: Tutankhamun's Iron Dagger
blurb: A blade made from a meteorite, found on the boy king's mummy. Was it a royal gift from another kingdom?

title: Ramesses II, the "Younger Memnon"
blurb: Walk around a colossal granite statue of Egypt's most famous pharaoh and ask how rulers used monuments as propaganda.

title: The Rosetta Stone
blurb: Find the three scripts on the stone that unlocked Egyptian hieroglyphs, and debate where it belongs today.

title: Cleopatra VII
blurb: Turn a real scan of her portrait, read the clues in her headband and hairstyle, and ask who shaped her story.

title: An Indus Unicorn Seal
blurb: Examine a tiny stone seal carved with a one-horned animal and a script that no one can read yet.

title: The "Priest-King" of Mohenjo-daro
blurb: Study the most famous statue of the Indus cities, a civilization with no known palaces or royal tombs, and decide whether he was really a king.

title: A Shang Oracle Bone
blurb: Turn over a bone the Shang kings cracked with fire to question their ancestors, carved with the earliest Chinese writing.

title: A Shang Bronze Helmet
blurb: Turn a bronze war helmet with a monster face on its brow, and ask who in a Shang army could afford one.

title: A Shang Ritual Cauldron (Ding)
blurb: Look for hidden faces on a bronze vessel used to feed the ancestors, and discover what bronze meant for Shang power.

title: A Shang Ceremonial Axe (Yue)
blurb: Face a grinning bronze axe from a great Shang tomb, a weapon that stood for the power to command and punish.
